title: Neon Harbour
blurb: A missing courier, a waterfront of lies, and a club where everybody knows the password but you.

office.title: The Retainer
office.prose: Rain on the office glass. The client's photograph shows a courier, a sealed case, and the harbour clock at eleven. "Find the case," she says. "Don't open it."

choices.text: Take the retainer and the photograph

pier.title: Pier Nine
pier.prose: Pier Nine stinks of diesel and low tide. A dockhand watches you from under a lamp, and a skiff knocks against the pilings below.

choices.text: Ask the dockhand about the courier

skiff.title: The Skiff
skiff.prose: The skiff is empty but for a crushed matchbook from The Glass Eel and a smell of expensive smoke. Someone left in a hurry.

choices.text: Pocket the matchbook and climb back

dockhand.title: The Lamp
dockhand.prose: "Courier? Tall, nervous, case chained to his wrist. They took him up to Marlow's warehouse, smiling." The dockhand holds out a hand, then shrugs and tells you anyway.

club.title: The Glass Eel
club.prose: The Glass Eel glows green through the rain. The singer stops mid-song when she sees the matchbook, and leans close: "Marlow's password is kingfisher. Spend your coin and I'll tell you which door."

choices.text: Buy her a drink for the door

warehouse.title: Marlow's Warehouse
warehouse.prose: Crates to the ceiling, one lamp, Marlow himself, and the courier tied to a chair — alive. "Say kingfisher and we talk," Marlow says. "Otherwise you're trespassing."

choices.text: Say the password and demand the case

roof.title: The Watcher
roof.prose: Gravel, a ventilator, and a watcher with a rifle who was never part of anyone's plan — yours, Marlow's, or the client's.

closed.title: Case Closed
closed.prose: "Kingfisher." Marlow laughs like a man outbid and hands over the case, still sealed. The courier walks out on his own feet. You never learn what was inside, and the cheque clears.

joined.title: The Payoff
joined.prose: The money is real and heavy and wrong. You spend it all over town for a year and never once stop hearing the harbour clock strike eleven.

setup.title: The Setup
setup.prose: The watcher was waiting for exactly that. The last thing you hear is the harbour clock striking eleven, right on schedule, like it was always going to.
